payload.feature:
Decision 0036 is accepted (ruled 2026-09-03; docs/decisions/0036-egress-is-a-property-of-the-route.md). Enact it. Read the decision first: each of its five rulings names an enforcement binding, and those bindings are this commission — nothing beyond them.

What to build:

1. An `EgressClass` enum — local, contracted, uncontracted — in brokkr-runtime::agents beside TrustTier (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/agents.rs), parsed in agents::load with the same closed-vocabulary refusal naming the file and the key, defaulting to uncontracted on absence (ruling 1). The vocabulary is the engine's; which route belongs to which class is operator data.

2. `Adapter` gains `routes: Map<String, EgressClass>` and agents::load gains a route resolver (ruling 2): a concrete model id of the form <route>/<model> resolves to that route's declared class; an id with no prefix resolves to the adapter's own declared class and no better; an adapter fronting a single destination declares one class at the adapter and no routes. Driver conformance tests cover the prefixed, unprefixed and undeclared-route cases, and the unprefixed case asserts it does not inherit a better class than the adapter's own.

3. Local is structural (ruling 3): the gate-seat refusal in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs (today at line 1056) keeps reading trust_tier alone. A test seats a local, untrusted route at a gate and asserts the refusal is unchanged.

4. Secret bindings key off the class (ruling 4). A seat declaring bindings (decision 0012) compile-refuses unless its resolved route's class meets a minimum the operator rules into the bundle — a plainly named bundle-level key whose default is contracted, so every bundle on disk keeps its present behaviour. `binding_grant` is superseded: a true grant reads as contracted, a false or absent grant as uncontracted, and the old key stays readable one release so no adapter file is forced to change. Rewrite the existing 0021 ruling 4 compile refusal against the class comparison, keep its fail-closed tests, and add a migration test asserting the five adapters as they stand (claude, codex, dsh, exec, lanetally) resolve to exactly the clearances they have now. Assign no route to a class in adapter data: spark is not ruled local by this slice, and dsh's routes map, if you add the key at all, carries only values that leave every route where it stands.

5. `brokkr doctor` reports, per route, when a declared credential variable is satisfied from the process environment rather than the bindings store, named as a warn by route name (ruling 5). The ambient channel is not forbidden; it stops being invisible.

Do not touch: the wire protocol (egress is compile-time policy and never reaches forge-driver/v1), any journal row, the tier vocabulary, or decision 0021 rulings 2, 3 and 7. Bundle digests move only where a route class is declared — with no route declared, the witness pins in crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/witness_digests.rs and crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/compose_tests.rs should not move; if one does, name the reason in the commit. Full gate as the verify seat knows it, exact coverage included; every new refusal has a test that trips it.

result.notes: Framed the 0036 enactment in .forge/tasks/egress-class-enactment.md: EgressClass enum + adapter routes map + route resolver (rulings 1-2) in agents.rs/load.rs, ruling-4 refusal rewritten against class comparison with a new bundle-level minimum key in bundle.rs, gate-seat refusal at bundle.rs:1056 left untouched (ruling 3), doctor ambient-credential warn (ruling 5) flagged as needing a new credential-name data shape that doesn't exist yet. Non-goals and constitutional constraints (frozen phase-machine.json/reference/, no wire-protocol or journal changes, no route assigned a class in adapter data) spelled out explicitly.

Decision 0036 enacted, commit 35f68e0 on slice-egress-enact, all five enforcement bindings and nothing beyond them. (1) EgressClass {local, contracted, uncontracted} in brokkr-runtime::agents beside TrustTier, parsed in agents::load with the closed-vocabulary refusal naming file and key, absent = uncontracted. (2) Adapter gains routes: BTreeMap<String, EgressClass> and agents::load::resolve_route: a <route>/<model> id resolves to that route's class; an undeclared prefix and an unprefixed id both resolve to the adapter's own class and no better; tests cover the prefixed, unprefixed and undeclared-route cases and assert the unprefixed case inherits nothing better. (3) The gate refusal in bundle.rs still reads trust_tier alone; a test seats a local, untrusted route at a gate and asserts the refusal is unchanged, and that no egress word appears in it. (4) The 0021 ruling 4 compile refusal is rewritten against the class comparison with a bundle-level 'egress_minimum' (default contracted); binding_grant still reads one release (true = contracted, false/absent = uncontracted), declaring both keys refuses; every fail-closed test kept (assertions moved to the new message) plus a migration test pinning claude/codex/dsh/exec/lanetally at today's clearances and asserting every mapped model id, including dsh's three fronts, resolves where it stood. (5) brokkr doctor warns per route where an adapter-declared credential variable is satisfied from the process environment rather than the bindings store; --secrets-file names the store; adapters declare those variables by name under 'credentials'. No adapter file was edited and no route was assigned a class, so no bundle digest moved: witness_digests and compose_tests pins are untouched and recipes list prints the same digests. Gates: 934 tests green, --ignored empty, build --all-targets, clippy -D warnings, fmt, bundles/self and bundles/verify compile, recipes list, exact coverage 15385/15385 lines, 2340/2340 branches, 1449/1449 functions. Tree clean, nothing pushed. Not done, deliberately: crates/brokkr-cli/src/init.rs still scaffolds a new adapter with binding_grant: false — legal this release, but worth switching to 'egress' before the key is dropped.

cargo test --workspace: every test binary in the workspace reported 'test result: ok' with 0 failed (56 suites, 985 individual tests including brokkr-runtime's agents::tests, bundle::model_policy_tests, doctor::tests, and tests/witness_digests.rs — all green). cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: finished clean, printed a full manifest under the constitutional lint, digest 960b99d6f5c84a6943704132c94853034f0cc467947846549d41e0b66b411aae. Spot-checked decision 0036 enactment against the five rulings: EgressClass enum + closed-vocabulary load refusal (agents.rs, agents/tests.rs::the_library_loader_names_the_file_and_the_key_it_refuses-family); Adapter.routes + route resolver with prefixed/unprefixed/undeclared-route driver conformance tests (agents/tests.rs::a_route_prefix_resolves_a_class_and_an_unprefixed_id_inherits_nothing_better); ruling 3's structural-local gate refusal unchanged, reading trust_tier alone (bundle.rs:1118, model_policy_tests.rs::a_local_route_earns_no_gate_seat asserts a local+untrusted route at a gate still refuses on tier and the refusal never mentions egress); ruling 4's rewritten compile refusal against the class comparison with fail-closed tests plus the required migration test (model_policy_tests.rs::the_shipped_adapters_declare_what_decision_0021_ruled, asserting claude/codex/dsh/exec/lanetally keep exactly their present clearances); ruling 5's doctor per-route ambient-credential warn (doctor.rs::report_ambient_credentials, doctor/tests.rs::doctor_names_every_route_taking_its_credential_from_the_ambient_environment). Confirmed the 'do not touch' boundary: git diff 9f82777..HEAD --stat shows only ARCHITECTURE.md, doctor.rs/tests, cli/lib.rs, agents.rs/load.rs/tests.rs, bundle.rs/model_policy_tests.rs, runtime lib.rs re-exports, decision docs and two guides — no forge-driver wire protocol, no journal row, no TrustTier vocabulary change, and crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/witness_digests.rs plus src/bundle/compose_tests.rs are byte-identical to pre-slice (no route declared on any shipped adapter, so no digest moved), consistent with the commission. One honest run; nothing softened.

Reviewed 35f68e0 (the whole run: one commit against pre-run bbd01f4) on all three dimensions. The enactment matches its commission closely: EgressClass is a closed ordered vocabulary refused at load naming file and key (ruling 1); Adapter carries routes + credentials and agents::load::resolve_route implements ruling 2; the gate refusal still reads trust_tier alone and a local/untrusted route at a gate is pinned as refusing with no mention of egress (ruling 3); the ruling-4 refusal is rewritten as `egress < minimum` against a bundle `egress_minimum` defaulting to contracted, binding_grant still reads (true=contracted, false/absent=uncontracted) and declaring both keys refuses, and the five-adapter migration test pins every shipped model id including dsh's three fronts (ruling 4); doctor warns per route (ruling 5). No adapter file changed, no route was assigned a class, the wire protocol and journal rows are untouched, and the witness/compose digest pins did not move. I re-ran the gate from the worktree myself: cargo test --workspace green, clippy -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --check clean. Verified independently that the two panic-adjacent additions are unreachable (every Candidate comes from resolve(), whose entries all have a provider, so adapters.serving().expect() cannot fire) and that pinned_model preserves command_pins_model's exact 0031 semantics arm for arm. egress_minimum rides the bundle digest because the manifest hashes bundle.json's bytes, so the operator's bar is pinned into run identity.

FIXES APPLIED (commit ba3cb20, prose only, no digest moves, all gates re-run green): (1) ARCHITECTURE.md — rewrapped the paragraph the enactment left at 94 columns, no words changed; (2) docs/guides/contributing-by-hand.md — the guide tells a contributor to start from a file in adapters/, and all five of those still declare binding_grant, so following the new egress instructions as written produces the both-keys load refusal; the guide now says the old key is superseded-but-read and that declaring both refuses; (3) docs/guides/provider-adapters.md — the one page that tells the operator to keep DEEPSEEK_API_KEY/DASHSCOPE_API_KEY in the launching environment now names the `credentials` map and the ruling-5 doctor warn, which is precisely the channel that page recommends.

RESIDUAL FINDINGS, not fixed:

[medium, SECURITY] agents/load.rs resolve_route: a model id whose prefix the adapter does NOT name resolves to the adapter's own class rather than to uncontracted. Ruling 1 says "uncontracted is everything else, and is the value of an absent declaration", and an undeclared route is an absent declaration; unlike the unprefixed case (where the id genuinely does reach the adapter's own default destination, which is ruling 2's stated rationale) a prefixed-but-undeclared id names a destination the machine positively knows is NOT the adapter's own. Failure scenario: the operator declares dsh `egress: "contracted"` (having ruled DeepSeek's default route acceptable) and `routes: {"spark": "local"}`; `dashscope/qwen3.8-max` — Alibaba, never ruled — then resolves contracted, clears the default egress_minimum, and a seat may bind a secret toward it. That is the fail-open the decision's own rejected alternative 1 exists to prevent ("granting dsh the binding grant clears the Alibaba and DeepSeek routes at the same stroke"). NOT exploitable on today's data: dsh, codex and lanetally are uncontracted, and claude/exec declare no routes. The behaviour is deliberate, documented in the commit message, and pinned by a test (an_agent_chains_route_resolves_through_the_adapter_that_maps_it exercises exactly this path with a contracted adapter), and the task framing permitted a documented alternative reading — so this is a policy reading for the table, not a fix a review seat should flip.

[info] bundle.rs pinned_model only recognises a literal `--model`/`--model=` at an inline site; anything else (an ambiguous double pin, a provider whose flag differs) yields "" and so resolves to the adapter's own class. Harmless today because 0031's pin requirement refuses such a bundle anyway — but enforce_model_policy runs BEFORE enforce_model_pins in the same compile, so the egress check passes on the wrong destination first and the two rulings are now coupled: relaxing 0031's pin rule would silently widen this one.

[info] `routes` and `credentials` keys are validated against the name grammar but never against the adapter's own model-id prefixes, which are in the same file. A misspelled `routes: {"sparc": "local"}` is a silent dead declaration leaving spark/* at the adapter's class (fail-closed, but silent, against this loader's own stated "a misspelled class must never read as uncontracted by accident" idiom), and a misspelled credentials key produces a doctor warn naming a route that does not exist.

[info] recipes/wager-harness/README.md:88 still explains the mechanism as "binding_grant stays false". I fixed it, found that it moves the wager-harness manifest digest and trips witness_digests.rs, and reverted — a prose sweep inside a witnessed bundle directory needs its own commit with the digest move named, which is not this slice's commission. Flagged so it is not lost.
